answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to periodically submit a unique, assayed physical sample of basalt, jade, or cedar that is then permanently consumed in a public verification furnace. The sample's elemental fingerprint is recorded on-chain and cannot be reused. An attacker creating many identities must continuously source and destroy real quantities of these materials, incurring escalating procurement, shipping, and assay costs that scale linearly with the number of sybils, while honest agents need only one sample per identity lifetime.
